A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP/OpenCLIP bias audit. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V5 reports original FairFace and PATA bias measurements, debiasing comparisons, and neutral-image, calibration, and prompt-robustness results.

after.justification: V6 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: The model architectures, contrastive objective, and Bias Prompts, Prompt Array, and SANER mechanisms are unchanged. The revised probing description concerns the evaluation protocol assessed under E3.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same FairFace and PATA coverage, training corpora, 19 neutral-image controls, and crime/non-human, communion, and agency tasks. No dataset, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains Bias Prompts for CLIP and Bias Prompts, Prompt Array, and SANER for OpenCLIP. The baseline checkpoint comparisons in Table 1 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 replaces demographic labels concatenated with criminal/animal terms with comparisons between Crime-Related and Non-Human prompt sets, using within-set pooling, normally max, without concatenation. This revises the stated testing procedure. Appendix D already listed the separate prompts in v5, and no experimental rerun is documented.

E4.justification: The factor and mitigation analyses remain unchanged. Appendices A–C retain the same neutral-image sanity check, directional-bias calibration, and three-template PATA robustness analysis, with identical evidence.

E5.justification: The 95% bootstrap confidence-interval reporting in Figures 1 and 4 and the appendix mean/standard-deviation reporting are retained. No seed, repeated-run, or statistical estimation information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and Figures 1–10 retain their numerical results and findings. For example, Table 1 still reports FairFace CLIP B/32 gender-crime skew of 1.19 and negative-communion frequency of 62%. The revised protocol description is not accompanied by revised results.

T1.justification: The loss, bias metrics, and calibration definitions are unchanged. Section 3.4 replaces a malformed indicator glyph with 1 without changing the mathematical meaning; no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-data source, scaling effects, and the source- and size-dependent effectiveness of debiasing.

C2.justification: The discussion, substantive limitations, and appendix interpretations are retained, including demographic restrictions, proprietary-data limitations, and possible dataset overlap. Appendix B's interpretation moves relative to Table 6 without changing meaning.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 replaces the redacted code URL with an explicit repository address. Section 3.3 additionally specifies default max pooling. Existing hardware, training budgets, hyperparameters, and appendix prompt lists remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. The new publication notice and OpenReview link provide publication metadata.

P1.justification: V6 locally rewrites the crime/non-human paragraph, removes the unresolved section reference in Section 3.6, adds acknowledgements and publication information, and makes small spacing corrections. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Publication headers and added text cause limited layout reflow, including relocation of Figures 9–10 and placement of Table 6 before its interpretation. Existing figure designs, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V6 makes the probing description more explicit and better aligned with Appendix D's existing prompt sets, supplies the previously redacted code address, and fixes indicator typesetting and a broken reference. These provide limited gains in clarity and reproducibility information. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish a rerun under the revised protocol description.
